paragraphs.text: Now that they had heard the law, received the sacrament, and had their hearts filled with the joy of the Lord, which was their strength, and graciously lifted up in the Lord’s ways, as 2Ch 17:6, they returned not home, till they had first done these zealous acts.
paragraphs.anchor: Now when all this was finished.

paragraphs.text: They with their king. {2Ki 18:4}
paragraphs.anchor: And brake the images in pieces.

paragraphs.text: Such cities therein as were subject to Hezekiah. Or if they went further, they looked upon Hoshea then king of Israel as a usurper: and he being rather an atheist than idolater, suffered the people haply to do herein as they would, so that he might be suffered to sit in the throne.
paragraphs.anchor: In Ephraim also and Manasseh.

paragraphs.text: They did not cast off their callings, and all care of their affairs, now that they were enlightened, as some of our sectaries hold themselves bound to do.
paragraphs.anchor: Returned every man to his possession.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Of the temple, fitly compared to a camp, for the watch and ward there kept by the priests, and for the convention of the people thither, as to their rendezvous, to pray, which is the chief service of our spiritual warfare.
paragraphs.anchor: In the gates of the tents of the Lord

paragraphs.text: He appointed also the king’s portion of his substance.] That is, Of his proper goods, and at his own particular cost. This he did of his princely liberality, for the ease of the people, who had been miserably peeled out and impoverished in his father’s days.
That having των αναγκαιων χωρηγιαν, as Chrysostom hath it, a liberal subsistence, they might serve the Lord without distraction, and with much alacrity: for
paragraphs.anchor: That they might be encouraged.

paragraphs.text: “ Pluribus intentus minor est ad singula sensus. ”

Heb., Brake forth. Ahaz had nulled the laws for ministers’ maintenance, that he might bring them to beggary and dishearten them - the like did Julian the apostate; - Hezekiah therefore reviveth those laws with the first: and the people readily obeyeth them.
paragraphs.anchor: And as soon as the commandment came abroad.

paragraphs.text: {a} Not pinchingly and deceitfully, as now-a-days. Spoliantur Parochiae et Scholae non aliter ac si fame necare nes velint, saith Luther. Our parishes and schools are so robbed of their right, as if they meant to famish us all. {b} To colour the matter, conscience is pretended by some: but the apostle telleth them it is not conscience, but covetousness. {2Co 9:5}
paragraphs.anchor: Brought they in abundantly.

paragraphs.text: {a} Libenter et liberaliter.
{b} Maligne dantibas maledicit Deus {Mal 3:9}
i.e., Such as, over and above the tithes ordinarily appointed to be paid, any did voluntarily vow to give: so the Vulgate. See 2Ch 31:8.
paragraphs.anchor: Which were consecrated unto the Lord

paragraphs.text: About pentecost which is called the feast of harvest.
paragraphs.anchor: In the third month.

paragraphs.text: That is, Of the grain stacks, brought by the people into the tithe barns. {Mal 3:10} This they did not, till the king both exhorted them, and began to them.
paragraphs.anchor: They began to lay the foundation of the heaps.

paragraphs.text: About the feast of tabernacles, called the feast of ingathering at the end of the year. {Exo 23:16}
paragraphs.anchor: And finished them in the seventh month.

paragraphs.text: For so good a year; but especially for so good a frame of spirit in the people.
paragraphs.anchor: They blessed the Lord.

paragraphs.text: See on 2Ch 31:7.
paragraphs.anchor: Concerning the heaps.

paragraphs.text: The same, saith Lyra, that withstood Uzziah, with so much zeal and courage.
paragraphs.anchor: And Azariah the chief priest.

paragraphs.text: That is, His priests and people, saith Lavater, who have rightly used and not wasted God’s plenty.
paragraphs.anchor: For the Lord hath blessed his people.

paragraphs.text: Or, Storehouses. Prepared they were before by Solomon: but now they were put in order, and made fit for such a use.
paragraphs.anchor: To prepare chambers.

paragraphs.text: Sin offerings and thank offerings.
paragraphs.anchor: And brought in the offerings.

paragraphs.text: See on 2Ch 31:6. Among our forefathers, the statute of Mortmain provided they should give no more to the church. But now there needed no such statute; the springs of men’s bounty being like Jordan turned back.
paragraphs.anchor: And the dedicated things.

paragraphs.text: Heb., In truth: they paid their dues honestly and out of conscience: not counting all well got that was gotten from the priests, as now-a-days they do.
paragraphs.anchor: Faithfully.

paragraphs.text: Without whose advice the king would do nothing in church affairs. The great Turk doth the like with his mufti, {A Muslim priest or expounder of the law} &c.
paragraphs.anchor: At the commandment of Hezekiah the king, and Azariah.

paragraphs.text: Super liberalitates Dei, called also the most holy things or sanctities of sanctities. See 2Ch 31:6.
paragraphs.anchor: Was over the freewill offerings of God.

paragraphs.text: In a geometrical proportion.
paragraphs.anchor: To give to their brethren by courses.

paragraphs.text: For these also there was maintenance allotted and allowed: so great was the abundance of the offerings, the people’s liberality, and the king’s providence, piety, and devotion.
paragraphs.anchor: From three years old.

paragraphs.text: Their wives and children depended upon them for a maintenance, and had it.
paragraphs.anchor: Of all their little ones, their wives, &c.

paragraphs.text: This his uprightness was the best stake in his hedge, when the news of death made all crack. {Isa 38:3}
paragraphs.anchor: And wrought that which was good, &c.
